COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
C528 No. 136 of 2024
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Abhishek Verma, learned counsel 
for the applicants.
2. By the instant criminal miscellaneous 
application preferred under Section 528 of 
BNSS 2023, the applicants are challenging 
the proceedings of Complaint Case No. 3194 
of 2020 filed by the respondent/complainant 
in which the applicants have been 
summoned for the offences punishable 
under Sections 498A, 323 and 504 IPC read 
with Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. The brief facts of the case are that 
applicant no. 1 married with respondent/ 
complainant on 10.02.2019 and from this 
wedlock one child was born. In para 9 it is 
stated that there are possibilities of 
amicable settlement and prior to that so 
many attempts were made but applicant no. 
1 could not succeed. 
4. After taking into consideration the 
averments made in para 9 of the petition,
this Court is of the view that efforts may be 
made for their amicable settlement.
5. Issue notice to respondent.
6. Learned counsel for the applicants 
shall take steps to serve respondent within 
three days by both mode including 
electronic mode as well as through the 
counsel representing the respondent in the 
trial court.
7. List this case on 20.08.2024.
8. On that day applicant no. 1 and 
respondent shall remain present in Court for  the purpose of their amicable settlement.
9. Till the next date of listing, further 
proceedings of Complaint Case No. 3194 of 
2020, pending in the court of Judicial 
Magistrate/1st Addl. Civil Judge (J.D) 
Roorkee District Haridwar for the offences 
punishable under Sections 498A, 323 and 
504 IPC read with Section 4 of Dowry 
Prohibition Act shall remain stayed.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
 30.07.2024 
Parul

05.05.2025 C-528 No. 136 of 2024
Hon’ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
Mr. Abhishek Verma, learned counsel for 
the petitioners.
2. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for 
respondent.
3. Learned counsel for the parties would 
submit that there are possibilities of amicable 
settlement between the parties.
4. The matter is referred for mediation.
5. In view of the above, let the parties appear 
before the District Legal Services Authority, 
District Haridwar on 14.05.2025 at 11.00 A.M. for 
conciliation.
7. The Secretary, District Legal Services 
Authority, District Haridwar shall appoint a 
Mediator for conciliation proceedings of the 
parties.
The Mediator shall file report before this 
Court through Secretary, District Legal Services 
Authority, District Haridwar.
8. List this case on 26.06.2025 alongwith 
report of the Mediator.
9. Learned counsel for the respective parties 
shall ensure the presence of the parties on 
14.05.2025 before the District Legal Services 
Authority, District Haridwar for conciliation.
10. Let a copy of this order be sent to the 
Secretary, District Legal Services Authority, 
District Haridwar for necessary compliance.
11. Interim order dated 30.07.2024 to continue 
till the next date of listing.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
C-528 No. 136 of 2024
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
Mr. Abhishek Verma, learned counsel for the Applicants. 
2. Mr. Tapan Singh, learned counsel for the Respondent. 
3. As per the order sheet dated 05.05.2025, passed by the 
learned Coordinate Bench, the parties were directed to appear 
before the District Legal Services Authority, District Haridwar, on 
14.05.2025 at the specified time. Further directions were issued 
for the District Legal Services Authority, District Haridwar to 
appoint a Mediator for the conciliation proceedings between the 
parties. It was also directed that the Mediator would submit a 
report to this Court through the Secretary, District Legal Services 
Authority, Haridwar. The matter was accordingly listed for today 
along with the report of the Mediator.
4. Learned counsel for the Respondent states that the 
Applicants never appeared before the Mediator at the District 
Legal Services Authority, Haridwar, and consequently, the 
mediation proceedings could not take place.
5. It appears, based on the conduct of the parties, that the 
mediation process cannot proceed and is deemed to have failed.
6. List this case on 18.07.2025.
7. In the meantime, if so desired, rejoinder affidavit on behalf 
of the Applicants may be filed.
8. Interim order, if any, is extended till the next date of listing.
 (Ashish Naithani, J.) 
 26.06.2025
